population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 46.5 − current 37.3 = 9.2% of adults have used and are off now; of the 2032 on-drug 27.9, 65% (18.1) stayed on, 9.8 stopped and joined the 9.1 already off (pool 18.9), of whom 58% (10.9) restarted, so the 2032 ever-users split into 18.1 + 10.9 = 29.0 on and 8.0 off; the 9.5 pts of new ever-users split into 8.3 on and 1.2 off, giving 29.0 + 8.3 = 37.3 on and 8.0 + 1.2 = 9.2 off; cyclers = 13.4 (by 2032) + ~5.5 first-time restarters + ~0.3 among new starters = 19.2 of 46.5 = 41%. Persistence rose from 60% to 65% because generic semaglutide at $39–69 cash removed price as a reason to stop. Restart stayed near 57–58%. Users ≈ 100.7M of ~270M adults. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 4.70 + 13.20 + 13.20 + 6.21 = 37.31. Income thirds: (41 + 37 + 33.9)/3 = 37.3. The bottom third rose most, 21.7 → 33.9, because Medicaid coverage of generic incretins became mandatory in 2034 (it had been optional) and HRSA switched to generic semaglutide. Most of that use is generic semaglutide, not triple agonists. The 65+ band rose 17 → 27 (~16.8M) once the Bridge became a permanent Part D benefit with $10 generic copays and the dementia-risk label kept pulling people in. Off-drug: ~24.8M adults have used and stopped. More of them now stopped by choice (GI effects, pregnancy, the grey, principle) than were cut off, because a person dropped by a conditioned plan can buy the generic for $49. ~144M (53.5%) have never used: organised refusers, people with contraindications, the uninsured in non-expansion states who missed Medicaid work-requirement reporting, and people who simply never wanted it. Pediatric: 1.9% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 1.39M, of whom ~230k are aged 6–11, mostly on generic liraglutide or off-label generic semaglutide. Children born in 2023 are now eleven and have never known a family table without at least one adult on a pen.

access.public_coverage: Public programmes are now the largest payer: 45% of fills, ≈45.3M users. MEDICARE: the Dec 2033 Medicare and Medicaid Metabolic Health Act replaced the Bridge (which expired 31 Dec 2033) with a permanent Part D obesity benefit, generic-first. Generic semaglutide carries a $10 copay and branded agents need step therapy and a $50 copay. Conditions carried over for obesity-only beneficiaries: ≥5% loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, and baseline and annual DEXA plus a resistance-training referral for 65+. Medicare pays 18% of fills ≈ 18.1M users (≈16.8M aged 65+ plus ~1.3M disabled under 65). Blended net cost is 70% generic at $55 and 30% branded (tirzepatide, retatrutide, MariTide, CagriSema, amycretin) at $245: 0.7×55 + 0.3×245 = $112/month. 18.1M × $112 × 12 ≈ $24.3B/yr, about 2.2× the user count of 2032 at a similar order of spend. MEDICAID: the same Act removes generic incretins from the Section 1927(d)(2) optional-exclusion list, so every state must cover generic semaglutide and liraglutide for obesity from 1 Jan 2034. Branded agents remain optional. A new state-plan option lets states attach adherence and weigh-in conditions without an 1115 waiver, and 16 states use it, including the original seven waiver states. Medicaid pays 20% ≈ 20.1M users at a blended 80% generic $50 net and 20% branded $225: 0.8×50 + 0.2×225 = $85/month. 20.1M × $85 × 12 ≈ $20.5B/yr combined, down from $24.3B for 9.0M users in 2032. HRSA: the FY2034 appropriation is $2.4B, cut from $5.0B. Generic semaglutide replaces liraglutide for adults: 4.0M users (2.6M obesity, 1.4M cessation/AUD) × $45 × 12 ≈ $2.16B. The FY2034 rider adds a semiannual weigh-in for obesity patients. Cessation and AUD patients are exempt under 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality. TRICARE/VA/DoD: 3% ≈ 3.0M users, including ~190k active duty in the Metabolic Readiness Program at ~$60 generic DLA price: 190k × $60 × 12 ≈ $137M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month and several generic tirzepatides at $20–45. Brazil, Turkey, Mexico and Indonesia run on Indian and domestic generics. A Chinese originator GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist approved by the NMPA launched in Brazil, Indonesia and the Gulf states in 2034 at ~$90/month. Lilly's retatrutide launched in the EU, UK and Japan in 2033–34. Canadian generic semaglutide is ~C$60.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse: under the patent settlements, FDA-approved generic semaglutide injections (Teva, Viatris, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's, Apotex) launched in the US in March 2033. Novo answered with an authorised generic at $59. By late 2034 the pharmacy cash price is $39–69 a month, even after the Section 232 duty on Indian API, which adds about $4–6 per pen. Branded direct prices followed: Wegovy via NovoCare $99, the Wegovy pill $99, Foundayo $99, tirzepatide via TrumpRx $199 (still patent-protected, no US generic), retatrutide direct $349 and list $1,499. The Zepbound list price is unchanged and unpaid. Payer mix of ~100.7M users: commercial 31% (31.2M), Medicare 18% (18.1M), Medicaid 20% (20.1M), HRSA 4% (4.0M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3% (3.0M), cash/direct 17% (17.1M), gray 7% (7.0M) = 100%. Employer weight-management coverage rose 63% → 74% because generics made it cheap. 62% of covering employers attach conditions, though with $49 cash available the conditions protect a small subsidy, so many employers moved them onto premium differentials tied to biometric outcomes (waist, BMI, A1c), which apply whether or not the employee uses the plan's drug. Cash users rose to 17.1M, partly people opting out of conditioned plans to keep their dosing off PBM feeds. The 503A compounders lost their 'personalised' rationale once FDA-approved generics were commercially available, and most closed or moved to tirzepatide. Gray use fell from 9.0M to ~7.0M and is now mostly research-peptide retatrutide and tirzepatide, Indian mail tirzepatide, and people who want no record at all: pilots, service members, teenagers.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, plus US generics and Novo authorised generic from Mar 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; branded only in US)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance; Part D preferred for BMI ≥40 from 2034)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin dual agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Sep 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, incl. low-dose BED presentation)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, obesity with MASH)
Activin type II receptor antibody + tirzepatide co-pack (bimagrumab + tirzepatide, approved Feb 2034 narrowly for adults ≥60 with obesity and low lean mass)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
alcohol use disorder (semaglutide, Jun 2030; generics carry the label; ASAM/APA guideline first-line pharmacotherapy alongside naltrexone, Oct 2033)
reduction in risk of dementia in adults ≥55 with type 2 diabetes or obesity plus established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, Jun 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: generic semaglutide for AUD without obesity in DUI and drug courts as a probation condition (now on-label for AUD, but court-mandated adherence is the novelty)
tirzepatide and Foundayo for AUD, guideline-mentioned as second-line but unlabelled
'brain health' generic semaglutide for 50–65-year-olds outside the dementia label, now very cheap
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
gambling, compulsive shopping and cannabis reduction, still without a label
GLP-1 plus antiresorptive 'bone cover' in 65+, guideline-endorsed, Part D-covered
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen driver (triple agonist, ~30%) realised through an existing product in a new market position plus launches outside the US, as the envelope allows. Retatrutide (on market since before 2032; 12 mg maintenance gave 30.4% at 104 weeks) launched in the EU, UK and Japan in 2033–34. In Jan 2034 CMS placed it on the Part D preferred tier for BMI ≥40 or BMI ≥35 with comorbidity as a 'surgical alternative'. A Chinese originator triple agonist (NMPA-approved) launched in Brazil, Indonesia and the Gulf in 2034. It is not filed in the US. US bariatric surgery volume fell ~35% from 2032. Amycretin was approved Sep 2033 after its 2031 resubmission. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (BLA Mar 2032) was approved Feb 2034, narrowly, with a lean-mass label and limited uptake (~150k). AUD driver realised through guideline endorsement and generic inheritance of the 2030 semaglutide AUD label, not a new molecule. Lilly's tirzepatide and orforglipron AUD programmes are in phase 3 and not filed. Generic oral semaglutide is not yet available in the US because the SNAC formulation patents still apply. The global incretin market is ≈$150B in 2034, down from $165B: US volume rose ~35% but US net price fell ~45% as semaglutide went generic. Lilly's share rose and Novo's US revenue roughly halved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Some early generic-switch reports of 'worse nausea' were not confirmed in FDA's bioequivalence review and are attributed to patients restarting at full dose after gaps.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; generic labels identical.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed emptying on drug is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~74,000 filed and tolled claims. Generic manufacturers are largely shielded from failure-to-warn claims under the Mensing doctrine, so claims concentrate on brand-era use. Settlement talks are reported but no global deal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled; FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide's Part D preferred status for BMI ≥40; partly offset by fewer bariatric procedures.
The AUD population has a higher baseline risk. Registries of ~1.4M AUD users show no excess over matched naltrexone users. The MDL track continues.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; ASAM guideline advises lipase history review before starting in heavy drinkers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged in kind. Prevalence is growing in absolute terms as 65+ use rose to ~16.8M, and is worst among Medicaid and HRSA users without protein or training support.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings retained. Part D obesity benefit keeps the resistance-training referral. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide approved narrowly (Feb 2034). HRSA still has no requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose another ~3% over 2032–33 and appear to plateau in 2034 where antiresorptive cover is used. Modelled excess ≈ 16.8M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr × HR 0.35 ≈ 29,000/yr before bone cover; the observed excess is lower, at an estimated ~20,000, because ~40% of 65+ users are on antiresorptives. The adolescent bone-accrual interim is still unadjudicated.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warnings-section DEXA retained. Part D covers DEXA and antiresorptives. FDA pediatric labelling update still pending the final study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in AUD and DUI-court populations.

The NIH pragmatic REWARD trial (Mar 2034; 11,800 adults, blinded randomised withdrawal) found a clinically meaningful SHAPS shift in ~0.7 pp excess over placebo at standard semaglutide and tirzepatide doses and ~3 pp at retatrutide ≥8 mg. Most of the earlier 10–15% survey figure is attributed to baseline depression, regression and expectation. Deliberate dose holidays among long-term users fell from ~45% to ~24%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling revised (Jul 2034) to 'uncommon at maintenance doses; common at high-dose triple agonism'. The retatrutide Adverse Reactions entry is retained. The same pharmacology underpins the BED and AUD use.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fewer cut-off-driven regains now that a dropped patient can buy the generic at $49, but they persist among Medicaid members locked out under conditioned state plans in states where pharmacies report cash fills to the plan.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D signals persist. Thiamine is now watched in AUD users with low intake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling includes a protein target; ASAM adds thiamine advice.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult follow-up and eleven years in adolescents. ~230k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still not reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; bone-accrual final study due 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls fell ~30% as compounded semaglutide disappeared. Research-peptide retatrutide and tirzepatide harms persist among gym and teen users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP mail seizures continue; FDA ends compounding flexibility for semaglutide; two further distributor indictments.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; absolute cases up with wider retatrutide use.
Generic pricing accelerated 'brain health' use among 50–64-year-olds outside the label. These users carry bone risk without proven cognitive benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA labelling states population limits; Part D covers only on-label dementia-risk use, so overreach is mostly cash at $49.

food_and_beverage.state: With more than a third of adults on drug, US packaged-food volume falls ~3% a year. Snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks are hit hardest, and private-equity owners of divested indulgent brands begin consolidating plants in the Midwest. Protein, fibre and bone-and-muscle formats keep growing, and Medicaid nutrition-counselling contracts now specify protein targets. Grocery basket size is down but premium protein lifts revenue per trip at large grocers.

alcohol.state: Sixth straight year of US volume decline, with spirits and beer each down roughly 5–6% over the window. AUD guidance makes generic semaglutide a first-line prescription, and the effect is felt most in heavy-drinker volume, which the industry depends on. In Bardstown and Nelson County, Kentucky, bourbon producers pause distilling at several sites and cut rickhouse shifts as aging inventory outruns demand. Kentucky's barrel-tax receipts and several states' excise revenues miss forecasts. Non-alcoholic and low-dose formats grow but do not offset the decline.

restaurants.state: Buffet and value-volume chains in Ohio and Indiana close more units. Fast casual standardises 'half plates' and smaller-format stores. Bars lose late-night trade. Open Table suppers and church potlucks grow as gatherings but remain outside the restaurant economy.

apparel.state: Size runs remain wide and returns from rapid size change are a logistics cost. Uniform makers re-cut again for police and military. Hip-protector apparel is now Part D-adjacent merchandise in senior catalogues.

fitness.state: Resistance training is now a payer condition. Part D referrals, Medicaid state-plan conditions and employer biometric programmes feed low-cost gyms, physical-therapy chains and Medicare Advantage strength classes. Sun City, Arizona community gyms add evening sessions. The research-peptide gym trade persists at the margins.

insurance.state: Commercial pharmacy trend falls to ~+3% as semaglutide goes generic. Plans and employers shift conditions from drug access to biometric premium differentials. The Sixth Circuit upheld such differentials (Jun 2034); the Ninth Circuit is pending. Bariatric surgery claims are down ~35% from 2032. PBMs pivot from adherence-verification to biometric-verification services, including connected scales.

pharma.state: Lilly remains the tariff-exempt national champion and gains share on tirzepatide and retatrutide. Novo's US revenue roughly halves and it cuts US sales staff, leaning on amycretin and CagriSema. Generic makers win volume on thin margins and pay Section 232 duty on Indian API. MDL reserves remain. The overall global market shrinks in dollars while volume rises.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Leanness no longer signals money, because the generic costs $49. It now signals compliance: a lean body reads as one that passed the weigh-in, made the PDC and got the DEXA. A heavier body is read as either refusal or exclusion. Among the never-users, refusal is increasingly visible and organised.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle and bone remain the class markers. Retatrutide at $349, or Part D-preferred for BMI ≥40, makes 'surgical-grade' loss common in working-class Ohio and Kentucky, and 'pen-thin' is now said of anyone who lost weight without training. In Sun City, affluent women pay for trainers, protein and zoledronate; Medicaid dual-eligibles get a referral slip and generic semaglutide.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Open Table suppers, begun in Grand Rapids church networks, now run monthly in roughly 900 congregations, with a large Nashville 'Open Table Sunday' after the Sixth Circuit ruling. Oakland and Brooklyn fat-liberation groups host unmedicated supper clubs. Young evangelical women's 'natural appetite' circles in Tulsa treat finishing a plate as devotion. School nutritionists in Columbus write guidance for children whose parents eat a few bites at dinner.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On' or 'not on' is a routine profile field. 'Unmedicated' is a stated value in certain circles. Sobriety and incretin status now sit side by side, since for many the drug is how they stopped drinking. Couples renegotiate a shared life without wine.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is cheap to suppress and still contractual: payers treat it as a modifiable risk and courts treat it as a probation term for drinkers. The backlash keeps 'hunger is how we were made' and adds 'sobriety by injection is not repentance' from some pulpits, a line that divides the movement because many congregations host recovery meetings that use the drug. Appetite-liberty laws now exist in nine states. Their reach over self-insured plans is uncertain after the Sixth Circuit's ERISA preemption ruling.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The NIH REWARD trial (Mar 2034) put excess clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~0.7 pp at maintenance semaglutide or tirzepatide doses and ~3 pp at retatrutide ≥8 mg. FDA's Jul 2034 class revision calls it 'uncommon at maintenance doses'. Deliberate holidays among long-term users fell from ~45% to ~24%. Low-dose Foundayo for BED has ~1.3M users. 'Quiet' wellness subscriptions are below 0.5M.
interior_life.framing: An uncommon, dose-dependent side effect that clinicians screen for in a two-question check, and a therapeutic mechanism in BED and AUD. 'The grey' survives as dated slang and a stand-up callback, much as people still joke about 'Ozempic face'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers no longer discuss mood. Conditioned plans track waist and A1c rather than how anyone feels. Skip-but-fill persists among people on conditioned plans, but fewer bother, because the generic makes the plan's subsidy small. Army chaplains report fewer 'grey' complaints and more about sobriety without the barracks social life.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' festival passes fade as a marketing gimmick. The drug's cultural presence moves to the sober-curious scene: alcohol-free late-night venues in Austin and Denver, and comedy about having no hangovers rather than about feeling flat. Casino and sports-betting operators still cite softer handle among heavy bettors.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Dose holidays around conception remain routine because of labelling. Holidays for pleasure are less common. Sex therapists cite the REWARD trial to reassure rather than warn. Couples argue more about drinking than about the grey.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The grey has lost force as an argument, so the backlash coalition has moved to conditioning, DUI-court mandates and the HRSA weigh-in rider, which it calls 'pacification with paperwork'. Pro-access populists claim the $49 generic as a win, and candidates are asked about the generic price and Part D rather than whether they take holidays.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and pro-generic. FDA approved generic semaglutide on schedule, approved amycretin and the bimagrumab combination, and revised reward-blunting language downward. It acts on bone and muscle through labelling and payer conditions rather than restriction, and enforcement now targets research-peptide distributors, not users or compounders.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. The Dec 2033 Medicare and Medicaid Metabolic Health Act makes Part D obesity coverage permanent and generic Medicaid coverage mandatory. HRSA is cut to $2.4B. The ACA cessation mandate continues. The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program continues on generic supply.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning outlived the price rationale. Part D keeps response, PDC and DEXA conditions for obesity-only beneficiaries. Sixteen states condition Medicaid coverage via the new state-plan option, and Indiana and Arkansas keep their 1115 terms. HRSA now requires semiannual weigh-ins for obesity patients. Employers shift to biometric premium differentials, upheld by the Sixth Circuit in Jun 2034. DUI and drug courts in Ohio, Texas, Kentucky and Arizona impose generic semaglutide adherence, verified by pharmacy pickup, as a probation term for alcohol offences, on the model of earlier naltrexone mandates.
state.workforce_or_military: Readiness programme ~190k active duty, on generic semaglutide first-line and tirzepatide second-line. Body-composition separations are down ~40% from the 2030 baseline. Religious-accommodation requests number about 3,400 in total. Police and fire contracts in Phoenix, Houston and Chicago continue. FAA special issuance is routine on stable doses.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Lilly remains the Section 232 strategic-supply champion with tariff exemption and DPA financing, though generic semaglutide now undercuts the federal ceiling price the deal was built around. Indian API for US generics pays Section 232 duty. India's WTO dispute has reached the panel stage without a ruling. Novo still pays duty on Danish API, and US–Denmark friction persists. A Chinese triple agonist is competing in Global South markets.

events.event: Under the patent settlements, the first FDA-approved generic semaglutide injections from Teva, Viatris, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's and Apotex reach US pharmacies, and Novo launches an authorised generic at $59. By year-end, cash prices at chain pharmacies run $39–69 a month despite the Section 232 duty on Indian API.

The American Society of Addiction Medicine and the American Psychiatric Association issue a joint guideline naming semaglutide a first-line pharmacotherapy for alcohol use disorder alongside naltrexone. The VA adopts it within weeks, and DUI courts in Ohio, Texas and Kentucky begin writing pharmacy-verified pickup into probation terms.

Congress passes the Medicare and Medicaid Metabolic Health Act as the Bridge expires. It creates a permanent generic-first Part D obesity benefit ($10 generic copay) that keeps the response, adherence and DEXA conditions, makes generic incretins mandatory Medicaid covered drugs from January, and lets states add adherence and weigh-in conditions by state-plan amendment. Sixteen states file within six months.

CMS places retatrutide on the Part D preferred tier for beneficiaries with BMI ≥40 as a 'surgical alternative'. Lilly reports EU and Japan launches, and a Chinese originator triple agonist goes on sale in Brazil and Indonesia at about $90 a month. US bariatric programmes report case volumes down about a third from 2032.

The NIH REWARD randomised-withdrawal trial finds excess clinically meaningful anhedonia of under one percentage point at maintenance doses and about three points on high-dose retatrutide. FDA revises class labelling in July to call reward blunting 'uncommon at maintenance doses'.

The Sixth Circuit upholds employer biometric premium differentials under the 2031 tri-agency guidance and holds Tennessee's appetite-liberty law preempted for self-insured plans. The following Sunday, Open Table congregations in Nashville serve an estimated 40,000 people, and appetite-liberty bills advance in three more legislatures.

open_tensions: Conditioning has outlived its price logic. A dropped patient can buy generic semaglutide for $49, so plans have moved conditions onto biometric premiums, which bind people who never use the plan's drug. The Sixth Circuit has upheld that, the Ninth is pending, and the ERISA preemption of nine states' appetite-liberty laws is headed toward the Supreme Court.

Medicare is now the default payer for ~16.8M older users, covering the incretin, the DEXA and the antiresorptive. Hip fractures have plateaued only where bone cover is used, nobody has fracture-outcome data for the combination in people 75+, and dementia-label overreach among 50–64-year-olds is now cash-priced and invisible to Part D.

Lilly's national-champion bargain was built around a federal ceiling price that generic semaglutide now undercuts. Tirzepatide patents run to the mid-2030s, India's WTO panel could rule against the Section 232 duties that raise generic costs, and Novo's shrinking US business strains the duopoly the supply deal assumed.

Court-mandated semaglutide for drinkers, the HRSA weigh-in rider and falling excise revenue put AUD treatment at the centre of the 'pacification' argument. The recovery congregations that use the drug and the Open Table congregations that preach against it are often the same churches, and HRSA's FY2035 funding is unresolved.
still_true: Tirzepatide remains under US patent protection with no FDA-approved generic. Zepbound and Mounjaro are sold only as branded products, and the Zepbound list price is unchanged and almost never paid.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.
Eli Lilly remains the Section 232 'strategic supply' national champion, with tariff exemption and DPA Title III financing for its Virginia and Texas plants, and Novo still pays duty on Danish API.

prose.headline: Forty-Nine Dollars and a Weigh-In: The Drug Got Cheap. The Conditions Didn't.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 about a hundred million American adults take an incretin drug, more than one in three. The fight over price that defined the last decade ended at a pharmacy counter in March 2033, when the patent settlements ran out and generic semaglutide arrived from Teva, Viatris, Sandoz and the Indian majors. Novo launched its own authorised generic at $59 to keep some of the business. Within a year a month's supply cost between $39 and $69 at chain pharmacies, even with the tariff on Indian ingredients. Tirzepatide is still under patent and still branded, now $199 through the federal portal. Retatrutide, the triple agonist that takes off nearly a third of body weight, is $349, and Medicare now prefers it over surgery for people with a BMI over forty. Bariatric surgeons in Columbus and Louisville describe their waiting rooms as quiet.

When the Bridge expired in December 2033, Congress made it permanent. Medicare now covers obesity drugs as an ordinary Part D benefit, with a $10 copay on the generic, and every state Medicaid programme must cover generic incretins. Public programmes pay for nearly half of all fills, and the bottom income third, once the least medicated, has nearly caught up. The cost per patient fell faster than the rolls grew, so Medicaid covers twice as many users as in 2032 for less money.

The conditions survived the price collapse. Medicare still drops obesity-only patients who have not lost five percent by month six or who skip their bone scan. Sixteen states condition Medicaid coverage on weigh-ins and refill records, and the free clinics now weigh patients twice a year. A dropped patient can walk across the street and pay $49 for the drug, so the conditions no longer ration much. They mostly sort people into the compliant and the non-compliant. Employers worked this out and moved their conditions from the drug to the paycheck, setting premium differentials by waist measurement and blood sugar whatever the employee takes. In June the Sixth Circuit upheld that practice and held that Tennessee's appetite-liberty law cannot reach self-insured plans. The next Sunday, Open Table churches in Nashville fed forty thousand people at folding tables.

Alcohol is the new front. In October 2033 the addiction psychiatrists made semaglutide a first-line treatment for drinking. The VA followed, and so did the DUI courts: in Ohio, Kentucky and Texas, a pharmacy pickup record is now a probation term. Spirits volume has fallen for six years. In Bardstown, Kentucky, distilleries have paused production because the warehouses are full of bourbon nobody will need for a decade. Some pulpits call injected sobriety false repentance. Many of the same churches host recovery meetings where half the room is on the drug.

The bone problem has not gone away, but where older users take antiresorptives alongside the incretin, hip fractures have stopped climbing. Women in Sun City who can afford trainers and zoledronate stand straighter than women who got a referral slip. Leanness used to signal money. Now it signals compliance, and muscle signals money.

The flatness people called the grey has mostly faded from conversation. A large NIH trial found it real but uncommon at ordinary doses, concentrated in high-dose retatrutide, and the label was revised to say so. Fewer people take dose holidays, comedians have moved on to hangovers nobody gets anymore, and the backlash has moved its argument from the drug itself to the paperwork around it. From the outside the country looks thinner, soberer and more measured than at any time in living memory, and an increasing share of what it does with its body is recorded somewhere.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Wade Haskins wakes at five out of habit, though the rickhouse doesn't need him until ten now. Four days a week since March. The barrels sit there aging whether he turns them or not.

Thursday is pen day. He does it at the kitchen counter, left side of the belly, the generic in its plain white box with the Kentucky Medicaid sticker. Tammy is already making biscuits for the Open Table supper at Mill Creek Baptist. She makes them every week, and every week he eats one.

At nine he stops at the Kroger pharmacy on North Third. Pickup counts. The girl at the window scans his card and says, "You're all set for court, Mr. Haskins," like she says it to everybody, and she probably does. Nelson County's DUI docket runs through this counter.

At the rickhouse, Danny from the bottling line says the company's going to a three-site schedule. Nobody says layoffs. Danny lost forty pounds on tirzepatide and quit chewing. He says he isn't sure he's quit wanting to.

At lunch Wade eats half a sandwich and doesn't think about the rest of it. That's the strange part, the not thinking.

Kayleigh calls from the high school. The nurse weighed the whole PE class again. She is fifteen and furious and not on anything, and she wants him to know that.

At supper the fellowship hall smells like ham. Pastor Doug says grace, and something about hunger being how God made us. Wade bows his head. He hasn't had a drink in fourteen months. He takes a biscuit and eats the whole thing.
